B045-01.notes: product of 4 and (n+3) is 4(n+3); 5 less than it: 4(n+3)-5. B reverses the subtraction.

B045-02.notes: g slope (10-2)/2=4, intercept 2; f slope 3, intercept -4. g is greater in both.

B045-04.notes: sqrt20~4.47, sqrt200~14.14; integers 5..14 make 10. Off-by-one distractors 9 and 11; 180 counts 21..199.

B045-05.notes: C(6,2)=15; 30 ordered/2. C (12) and A (6) are distractors.

B045-07.notes: Same height from A, so area ratio = BD/BC = 6/15; 50*6/15=20. D (30) is area ADC.

B045-09.notes: 9*9*8=648 three-digit numbers have all digits different; 648/900=18/25. Common traps: 9*9*8/999, 0.9*0.9=81/100, or 10*9*8/1000. The leading-zero restriction trips many students.

B045-10.notes: Rewrite as 2x-y+1=0 and 2x-y+6=0; the distance is |6-1|/sqrt(5)=sqrt5. The trap is the vertical gap of 5 (C). Few ACT students know the formula or how to set up the perpendicular.
